messages.subject: argument to summarize columns
parts:
Dr. Niedballa,

You have helped me in the past to have the recordTable summarize certain columns (you included two new arguments in a workaround function; eventSummaryColumn & event SummaryFunction to determine Count_max, the maximum amount of individuals of one species observed during a given delta).  Thank you for this!  I am now investigating passage of animals through wildlife crossings (underpasses).  My goal is to determine if an individual or individuals enter(s) one side of the crossing and then exit(s) on the other side during a certain timeframe.  It would be incredibly helpful to have an additional column that summarizes the max count of animals that completed a passage event from one side to the other, given criteria for their motion (activity related to entering or exiting the crossing).  If this is something that you would be able to offer insight for, then I can provide additional details for the argument, along with a small sample dataset to your email.

I appreciate your feedback and direction for this!

-Michelle

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] argument to summarize columns
parts:
Hello,  

it seems that you wish to combine multiple pieces of information here, which the event... parameters are currently not suitable for.
Would you please be able to describe what you wish to achieve more formally, ideally in terms of metadata tags that you assign to your images, and how you wish to combine them? 

From what I see it would combine the number of unique individuals (requires ID column) that perform a certain action (requires one or more activity columns). That is currently not possible and probably tricky to generalize. And to be honest I currently don't have capacity to add such rather exotic functionality. 

My suggestion would be to create a record table with all records (minDeltaTime = 0) and then extract the information yourself. Tweaking the function camtrapR:::assessTemporalIndependence may help in that (see here), but I'm not sure about that.
https://github.com/jniedballa/camtrapR/blob/master/R/variousOtherHelperFunctions.R

If you could provide a little more detail then maybe I'll have another idea for how to help you.

Best regards,
Jürgen

parts:
Dr. Niedballa,

Thank you for your response!  Yes, absolutely- I’m happy to provide additional details.  It is a tricky situation, so I really appreciate your insight to determine if this is attainable.  And I understand if this is too specific to my question, or may not be beneficial for other researchers, or something that you are not able to commit to at this moment. 

I am evaluating mammalian use of wildlife crossings, which in this case, are underpasses with multiple cameras at a station.  My goal is to determine the maximum count of individuals per species with a passage event through the crossings given a certain delta.  I have already conducted temporal autocorrelations per species, per crossing, and determined that the deltas are species and crossing-specific.  I started investigating this process with IFTHEN statements in Excel.  I used a recordTable filtered at 0 min (so that I could use a species-specific delta.time.min) with the simplest criteria for passage (Motion as “Entering” on one side of the crossing and then x min later Motion as “Exiting” on the other side of the crossing) to explore if I would be able to achieve this.  The Motion column has “Entering”, “Exiting”, and “In the Area” as options. 

                  In short, I am able to achieve:

1)     Maximum count of individuals per species at four or more cameras with the camtrapR:::assessTemporalIndependence function (with arguments: minDeltaTime = 0; deltaTimeComparedTo = lastIndependentRecord; camerasIndependent = FALSE; eventSummaryColumn; eventSummaryFunction)

2)     I can then filter by delta.time.min in Excel using a species-specific temporal autocorrelation time (conversely, if I was not interested in achieving step 3 below, then I could choose a species-specific minDeltaTime based on each temporal autocorrelation time to use in the camtrapR:::assessTemporalIndependence function in step 1 and be done)

However, I am currently not able to:

3)     Adequately assess passage given the activity of the species (Motion) using IFTHEN statements in Excel with acceptable criteria for passage as:

a.      Entering then Exiting

b.     Entering then In the Area

c.      In the Area then Exiting

I’ve attached an example of my current attempt to complete this task in Excel (columns V through Y contain formulas and comments for explanation).  As you will see, my IFTHEN statements result in a true positive, a false negative, and a false positive for a crossing event (the first 43 records).  Please note that the formula also does not take into account that I would also accept Motion as “Entering” and then x min later Motion as “In the Area”, and also Motion as “In the Area” and then x min later Motion as “Exiting” as an acceptable passage event.  Therefore, I am curious if it is possible to include if else criteria in the camtrapR:::assessTemporalIndependence function to achieve all of the above WHILE incorporating an argument for movement (i.e., Motion)?  (I understand I would be generating a recordTable per species in this instance).  I am eager to try anything you suggest, but my coding skills are limited, so I appreciate your direction if you are willing to provide insight as to how to accomplish this!  I hope this explanation is clear, but please let me know if you would like additional details.

Thank you, again, for your time in reviewing this,

-Michelle
